title: Baklava
subtitle: Layered filo pastry with nuts and honey syrup
excerpt: Dozens of sheets of butter-brushed filo pastry layered with a spiced walnut and pistachio filling, baked until golden, then drenched immediately with a cold orange blossom and honey syrup that soaks in as it cools.

recipe.sourceNotes: Baklava is a layered nut-and-syrup pastry found across the Middle East, Greece, Turkey, and Central Asia, with strong claims to origination from Turkey (where it is associated with the Ottoman court kitchen at the Topkapi Palace) and from Greek, Arabic, and Persian traditions. The essential technique is consistent across all versions: layers of very thin filo (or yufka) pastry are buttered, layered with a nut filling, cut into portions before baking, and then immediately drenched with syrup as they come hot from the oven. The hot pastry absorbs the cold syrup to create the characteristic moist, crisp, sticky texture. The syrup must be cold when it goes on the hot pastry: the temperature differential is what ensures absorption.

recipeTools.notes: A 30 x 20 cm baking tin; the dimensions matter for matching to the filo sheets.

content.text: The hot-pastry-meets-cold-syrup rule is non-negotiable: this is what makes the baklava absorb the syrup properly. Make the syrup first so it has time to cool completely before the baklava comes out of the oven. Keep the filo sheets you are not working with covered with a damp cloth at all times: they dry out and crack within minutes of exposure to air. Work fast once you start buttering.

Make the syrup first: put the honey, sugar, water, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Heat gently until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened. Remove from the heat. Add the orange blossom water. Allow to cool completely.
Mix the walnuts, pistachios, cinnamon, and cardamom together. Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Brush a 30 x 20 cm baking tin generously with melted butter.

Layer 10 sheets of filo in the tin, brushing each sheet with melted butter before adding the next. Trim to fit if necessary. Spread the nut mixture evenly over the filo. Layer the remaining filo sheets on top, brushing each with butter.

Using a very sharp knife, cut the baklava all the way through into diamond or square shapes before baking. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden brown. Remove from the oven and immediately pour the cold syrup evenly over the entire surface. Leave to cool in the tin for at least 2 hours before serving. The baklava keeps well at room temperature for up to 5 days.
